approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would introduce an annual cost recovery levy for Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants.
The charge would apply to celebrants registered on or after 1 July in a financial year, with exemptions available through regulations.
The measure was originally part of a 2011-12 Budget announcement intended to start from 1 July 2013 but was delayed due to the previous bill not passing before Parliament was prorogued.
Imposes an annual celebrant registration charge on Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants.
Provides legislative authority for the government to recover the costs of regulating this group.
Allows for exemptions from the charge to be set out in regulations.
Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants, including those from independent religious organisations whose denominations are not proclaimed under section 26 of the Marriage Act.

Moved a bill to allow the government to charge Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants an annual registration fee, with a statutory limit of $600 indexed to the consumer price index. Said the actual charge for the 2014-15 financial year would be considerably lower, at $240.

Moved a bill introducing cost recovery for the Marriage Celebrants Program, noting that 71.9 per cent of Australian marriages were performed by civil celebrants in 2012. Said celebrant numbers had grown from 3,334 in 2003 to over 10,400, and proposed a $240 annual registration charge alongside other fees.

Referred the Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Registration Charge) Bill 2014 and the Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Bill 2014 to the Federation Chamber for further consideration, noting general agreement on the legislation.

Presented a report examining 22 bills and 42 legislative instruments for compatibility with human rights. Raised concerns that national uniform schemes negotiated through COAG can be agreed without formal human rights scrutiny, and sought an update on efforts to address this in drafting protocols for national legislation.

Introduced two marriage celebrant bills implementing cost-recovery fees from 1 July 2014, including a $600 registration application fee, a $240 annual celebrant registration charge, and a $30 fee for seeking an exemption, all indexed annually to CPI.
